clue.text: Possibly pressed it about such impertinence!

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of pressed and it may be arranged in some other order

parts.note: C, for circa, is the usual short form of about

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone who has pressed their luck with a rude remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges PRESSED and IT together with C (circa, 'about'). The exclamation mark leans on the outburst of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Disrespect is rudeness or lack of proper regard, the same thing as cheek.

clue.text: Representation in holding company

indicators.note: holding means the word in grips the other piece inside itself

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A depiction kept by a holding company.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is an image or likeness, a picture standing for something.

clue.text: Engineers getting the wrong answer

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Engineers come up with the incorrect solution.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a sharp reply, so a kind of answer.

clue.text: They'll give voice if ingress is difficult

indicators.note: is difficult suggests the letters of ingress are troubled into a new order

explanation.surface: People who will speak up if getting in is hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Singers are vocalists, people who use their voices to perform.

clue.text: Make all adjustments necessary in the current recession

indicators.note: recession, a going back, tells us to read the word for current from right to left

parts.note: a tide is a current of the sea

explanation.surface: Advice to adjust everything needed during the economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning present-day, but it is the noun, a flow of water: TIDE, turned back by 'recession' to give EDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise text is to make whatever corrections and changes it needs.

clue.text: A port of greater acidity

definitions.meaning: a harbour city in Morocco on the Strait of Gibraltar
more sharp or sour in taste, the comparative of a zesty adjective

explanation.surface: A harbour town that is more sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is the Moroccan port city, and the comparative adjective means sharper-tasting or more sour.

clue.text: Make provision for expansion

parts.note: read as planning ahead for growth, but it means fitting a garment with stretchy bands so it can expand

explanation.definitionFit: To fit stretchy material into clothing lets it expand around the body.

clue.text: Promise employment

definitions.meaning: a pledge, especially a pledge to marry
a job or hiring, as of a performer for a run of shows

explanation.definitionFit: A betrothal is a promise to marry, and a booked job or hiring is also called by this word.

clue.text: The e brotherhood left imprisoned

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'The e brotherhood left imprisoned' (4): the stray 'e' is garbled and no word supplies the CAN that L should go inside, so the clue is cut or misread; search found no other source.

clue.text: Happy in admitting nothing can give rise to argument

parts.note: content means satisfied or happy

indicators.note: admitting means letting the other piece in, so in holds it

parts.note: taken as written
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Being contented with having nothing may yet start a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Contention is dispute or disagreement, the matter of a quarrel.

clue.text: A Japanese girl in college is hardly unusual

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of letters college is hardly

explanation.surface: A Japanese woman at college is no rarity.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the words 'colleGE IS HArdly'; 'unusual' only completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese woman trained as a hostess and entertainer.

clue.text: Get the copper back on a horse!

parts.note: a penny, a copper coin, is abbreviated P
astern means backwards, towards the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: An order to haul the policeman back up onto his mount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but it is a copper coin, P for penny. The pastern is a part of a horse's leg, so it is found on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The pastern is the part of a horse's leg between fetlock and hoof, so it is a feature found on the animal.

clue.text: Orders to copy a direction given in the news

indicators.note: in puts the copy and the direction inside the word for the news

parts.note: the press is the news media
to crib is to copy another's work
E for east is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Instructions to reproduce a directive reported by the media.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who prescribes is ordering or directing a treatment, so the verb is a synonym for commands.

clue.text: Please try a change, but not all at once

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of please try a

explanation.surface: A request to try something different, though one bit at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things individually or apart means they are not done together.

clue.text: Only half will follow a celebrity with a clear conscience

indicators.note: will follow puts the half word after the celebrity

parts.note: a nob is a person of wealth or high standing, a celebrated toff

indicators.note: half takes the closing two letters of only's four

explanation.surface: Only half a crowd will trail a famous person, and with a clear conscience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' here is the second half of 'Only', and 'will follow' places it after the celebrity; a nob is British slang for a toff.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting honourably and with high principle leaves one with nothing to feel guilty about.

clue.text: A tree put to some use?

definitions.meaning: the sorb, a European tree of the rose family with small fruit
being of use or help, as in being put into operation

explanation.surface: Asking whether a tree might be made useful.
explanation.definitionFit: The sorb tree has this common name, and something in operation or being used is in this state.

clue.text: Puts up with egghead in the organisation

indicators.note: in places the head of egg inside the turned word
up, in a down clue, means the word puts reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the head of egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates an intellectual within the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like a brainy person, but it means the head of 'egg': E goes inside STUP, the word 'Puts' turned 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-up is an arrangement or structure, the way a body or system is organised.

clue.text: Like a judge needing new robes

indicators.note: new indicates the letters of robes take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A judge requiring fresh gowns.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the idiom 'as sober as a judge'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom sober as a judge describes someone serious and not drunk.

clue.text: Catch sight of Oriental agent

parts.note: E, for east, stands for Oriental
a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: Glimpsing an Eastern secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to see it, especially at a distance.

clue.text: Time for a little fruit

definitions.meaning: a day or appointment on the calendar
the small sweet fruit of a palm

explanation.definitionFit: A calendar day is a time, and the palm bears a small sweet fruit of this name.

clue.text: About to make much of a man

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
to laud is to praise highly

explanation.surface: Getting ready to make a fuss of a fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'About' is C and 'to make much of' is LAUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Claud is a male first name.

clue.text: Assured it's nice art, though bizarre

indicators.note: bizarre signals the letters of nice art are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is confident the attractive artwork is odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sure is being confident and convinced.

clue.text: Drink in the air

definitions.meaning: a swallow or gulp of liquid
a current of air felt in a room

explanation.definitionFit: A long swallow of liquid is a gulp, and a chilly current through a room is also called this.

clue.text: Bob is terse and without doubt retrospective

parts.note: curt means brief to the point of rudeness

indicators.note: retrospective, looking back, means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: yes is an affirmation given without doubt

explanation.surface: A man called Bob is brusque and certainly looks back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name, but it is a bob of the knees; 'retrospective' turns the word for 'without doubt' back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a quick bend of the knees, the woman's respectful bow.

clue.text: There now!

definitions.meaning: in attendance, as a roll-call reply
at this time, the current moment

explanation.definitionFit: Someone attending is in this state, and the current moment is also given this name.

clue.text: Rather earlier

definitions.meaning: preferably, as in I would rather

explanation.definitionFit: The word means preferably, as in would rather, and also before in time.

clue.text: At home with diplomacy, so quite untouched

parts.note: in means at home
tact is diplomacy in dealing with people

explanation.surface: Someone comfortable with discretion, so wholly unaffected.
explanation.definitionFit: Something whole and undamaged has been left unharmed.

clue.text: A beast stacking up firearms

indicators.note: stacking up, in a down clue, means the word is piled from the bottom upwards

parts.note: gats is slang for guns

explanation.surface: An animal piling up guns.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer is an animal, a beast of the forest.

clue.text: River claims two lives

indicators.note: two means the word for lives is written twice

parts.note: is means exists or lives

explanation.surface: A river takes two lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lives' looks like the plural noun, but it is the verb: IS (exists). The Isis is the Thames as it flows through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isis is the name of the Thames at Oxford.

clue.text: A member of the opposition not against reform

indicators.note: reform tells us to form the letters of not against again in a new order

explanation.surface: An opposition politician who is not against reform.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is someone on the opposing side.

clue.text: Fish in a creel — seven or eight maybe

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits within the words creel seven

explanation.surface: A count of perhaps seven or eight fish in an angler's basket.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'creEL Seven'; 'or eight maybe' only fills out the angler's count. A creel is a fishing basket.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long snakelike fish.

clue.text: Suitable wear for a woman when retired

definitions.text: Suitable wear for a woman when retired

parts.words: Suitable wear for a woman when retired
parts.note: retired looks like having left work, but means having gone to bed

explanation.definitionFit: This garment is what a woman wears in bed at night.
